matches.rationale: Ground truth concerns ambiguous token budget notation (e.g., '8+42BT') making compute allocation unclear. No finding addresses this specific notation ambiguity or the difficulty in interpreting overlapping/exclusive budget definitions.

Both identify the same issue in Table 1: 1B-320BT vs 4B-80BT comparison lacks proper compute normalization (FLOPs, steps), making the claimed equal-compute comparison misleading and potentially exaggerating smaller model advantages.
Ground truth concerns RL/SFT data overlap contradicting the stated disjoint dataset claim. No finding addresses data partitioning or overlap between RL and SFT datasets.

Ground truth concerns Abstract overselling CPT benefits while omitting plateaus and forgetting. Findings address other Abstract issues (open-sourcing claims, ethical omissions) but not the specific CPT effectiveness claim distortion.

Both identify fabricated/misattributed dataset references. Finding 5 specifically catches FineMath being wrongly attributed to reference [38] (FineWeb paper) when it should be [2] (SmolLM2), matching the ground truth's concern about falsified dataset citations.

Ground truth concerns missing ethical disclosures (IRB, consent, bias assessment) in Abstract and methods. No finding explicitly identifies the absence of ethical considerations, bias mitigation, or responsible AI discussion.

Ground truth concerns overgeneralization in Conclusion about scaling trends and ORM reliability without acknowledging limitations. No finding addresses the Conclusion's rhetorical overstatement or insufficient limitation acknowledgment.

Both identify the Abstract claiming full open-sourcing of all models/datasets/pipelines while later sections reveal incomplete or partial release, creating a misleading impression about reproducibility resources.

Both identify the 350K/400K RL performance drop issue. Ground truth notes missing experimental details (early stopping, truncation); Finding 10 identifies contradictory explanations (speculative 'unreported instabilities' vs. definitive 'response length' cause) for the same phenomenon.
Ground truth concerns missing bias/fairness assessment in methods sections. No finding addresses the absence of dataset bias mitigation or demographic representativeness discussion.

Both identify missing error bars/variance in Figure 1 results. Ground truth notes absence of statistical variance hiding fluctuations; Finding 13 identifies explicit hedging text admitting 'considerable fluctuations' and 'run-to-run variability not shown' around the saturation claims.
Ground truth concerns missing computational formula and normalization method for ORM score metric. No finding addresses the ORM score definition ambiguity or reproducibility issues.

Ground truth identifies takeaways claiming diminishing returns while ignoring performance degradation. Finding 7 catches Takeaway 9 contradicting body text on saturation points; Finding 13 identifies Takeaway 1 presenting noise as definitive degradation—both match the claim distortion issue.

Both identify Table 4 baseline comparison issues. Ground truth notes missing hyperparameter/evaluation details making comparisons non-rigorous; Finding 8 shows the text claim ('similar or slightly better') contradicts Table 4 data (EvoLM consistently worse), exposing comparison credibility problems.

Ground truth concerns only final checkpoints being studied, excluding intermediate checkpoint analysis and hiding mid-training dynamics. No finding addresses this specific experimental design limitation.

Both identify the contradiction between Section 4.1 stating intermediate checkpoints are poor surrogates and Section 3 relying on intermediate checkpoints for core results, creating an internal methodological inconsistency that undermines the paper's conclusions.

Ground truth concerns promotional rhetoric in Related Work ('recent success', 'demystifying') inflating novelty. No finding addresses the rhetorical tone or overstated contribution claims in the related work section.
Ground truth concerns missing responsible disclosure, misuse risks, and risk assessments in reproducibility appendices. No finding addresses the absence of responsible AI or model misuse discussion.
